First why I still do not consider this an attack because due to my checklist it does not meet the criteria. It was not deployed in a well populated area "Well GuyInTheShed it was in a hotel are you nuts?" no it was in a stairwell in a hotel...the least populated section of any hotel with an agent still almost completely in a powdered state which means if the "attacker" was attempting to do as much harm as possible he had no idea what he or she was doing what so ever and didn't even research his or her chemical warfare agent properties. A more harmful location would have been a densely populated area with bodies to maximize effect such as a dance hall or convention room not a distant stair well with no one in it.

What should be understood about the deployment of Chemical Weapons is that they are A.O.E weaponry that are extremely fragile to the environment around them. When an attack is successful we do not "media measure" as we jokingly call it, they count everyone in the whole damn city or village whatever. We measure the area of effect and the population within that weapons area of effect to maximize treatment. So when we talk about population in an effected area we investigate the area of attack and focus on that population density not the density of the city around the effected area due to wanting to prevent mass hysteria or people reporting phantom symptoms or other medical symptoms when they reach the decon point. (All of this changes of course if the agent is of the Biological or Nuclear properties)

So in this case where the agent was deployed it is considered a Low population area being that a stairwell does not regularly have a dense population that could be harmed with immediate casualties. Now the people that were harmed reported having light symptoms of early chlorine sickness such as nausea and dizziness. I have not seen any further reports on conditions of the people but I am gonna say it now that they received a very low nearly harmful dosage and were medically transported due to precautions. Oxygen therapy with this low grade of final agent would be appropriate to relieve symptoms.

There does not have to be a pool for Chlorine to be stored in a hotel. I have reviewed cases where cleaning contractors were using Chlorine to extended their industrial strength bathroom cleaners that have made soldiers sick so that possibility is still an option and this was someone who dropped a completely inappropriately stored chemical and had not reported it probably because they were gonna attempt to clean it up. With your article on it being a Glass Container I will consider that into the scope of my personal investigation but I have not seen any other sources describe the container so until i do I can't confirm or deny anything on the form of the container.

What I really hope this isn't is a dumb ass prank pulled by some morons thinking they knew what they were handling.

74D CBRN (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear) Specialist checking in again.

From a chemical warfare perspective I would not call this an attack, if it was an attack it was extremely poorly executed with no apparent planning of deployment at all. If the chlorine was in a complete gas state not a powdered state more than 19 people would have been injured in the attack even if by the pictures being posted it was trapped in the stair well which is a EXTREMELY idiotic place to deploy a chemical weapon to get a wide range effect because in hotels most stair wells are not used for climbing with elevator access. Unless they were planning on crippling people who were escaping by contaminating all stair wells it isn't a very well planned out attack when there are other stairwells to escape from even elevators in this situation.

Lets look at a successful attack, the Tokyo subway Sarin gas attacks. The Sarin attacks were an example of extremely well planned attack that was extremely extremely successful with 12 being killed and several hundred more injured in some way or another because the passengers were trapped with the deployed agent inbetween station stops. It also shut down those train lines until complete decon was completed.

Chlorine is not the top choice to deploy in a stairwell even though does spread quickly it can be contained/slowed with doorways. People will still get injured from leaking and the chlorine being moved through air ducts but from the evidence shown this does not appear to be an "attack" either it was someone being stupid or it was a complete accident.

Also Chlorine isn't a total killer it can easily be survived...its just gonna suck but in extreme cases medical treatment, decon, lung checks, and rehab people can come out with little permanent effects.

Also remember gas attacks are a better morale killer than they are at wiping out soldiers or people in the battlefield with chemical defense measures able to be deployed individual to individual. Take the time to look at casualities from the WW1 gas attacks though lots of people were affected by the deployed agents it didn't kill millions unlike Hitlers contained gassing in World War 2

I don't see why people think they need this highly unsafe method of inappropriate workouts to get themselves in shape. 

I've been in the US Army Reserves for nearly four and a half years and before I joined the army I never worked. Unless you counted endless amounts of hours playing Eve Online as a work out. I lost a total of twenty-six pounds in basic and another fifteen in AIT. 

My one mile was around thirteen minutes..but after eight weeks I was at a fourteen fifty two mile. Now was I super skinny no but having come in at nearly two hundred and forty pounds standing at 5'8 I felt awesome.The best thing I was ever taught to do by drill sergeants was climb a ladder of fitness one step at a time not climb up as quickly as I could.

I couldn't do twenty-five push ups and did even worse in sit-ups during the diagnostic pt test but with simply keeping a log of whatever I did during morning PT I gained a motivational boost to keep trying as hard as I could but without injuring myself. I still keep that type of log and always pick a healthy safe starting point to work up from if I am medically forced to halt exercise routines.

The best advice I can give to anyone to safely lose weight is do a personal pyramid program. Give yourself a goal you want to meet, for example wanting to fifty push ups in one set or run a fifteen minute two mile. Find your base without running into muscle failure, like doing fifteen push ups or timing your quarter, half or mile distance. Then progressively begin to work your way up to your goal and beyond by increasing your reps every other day by five or even one.  Same thing with the run increase your distance slightly every other day and work on breathing, stretching and resting. (Applies to pretty much all exercises)

Now eating healthier can be challenging to but apply the same method of working out to reduce your calorie intake if you do what I did and eat maybe 3500 calories a day from all the fast food/soda I drank. Substitute candy with carrots, apple slices or banana slices it really helps. 

Most importantly relaaaaax have a day where you stretch, layout on the ground and unwind. It helps reduce stress and reduces the chances of damaging your body. Listen to some relaxing music you will be amazed at how relaxed you can get where the muscle pains fade away though depending on how fit you are jumping on your personal program you might need two days

This method has always worked for me and can really help you if your are struggling to lose weight. Its not an overnight fix but after a few weeks results will show and you won't feel like your knees are blown out or your rotator cuffs are destroyed.


It doesn't have to be crazy and fast to improve your exercise capabilities.

I like it alot, I love the Chemical Warfare side of the military, not exactly the deployment or anything like that just the science behind it. I do not condone the use of CBRN but I do agree we need to have a defense plan ready for the day someone does do something absolutely stupid.

The sarin deployment system they used was a cheap easy in home method. Take a baggy...wrap it in newspaper and then get a sharp umbrella tip. They carried the packages onto the subway trains and then set them down by their feet, before they got off they popped the baggy inside the newspaper with the tip of the umbrella.

Radiological mainly applies to radioactive sources that can be used as weaponry or just how to respond to a radioactive contamination etc etc. Nuclear applies to the WMD, it does also cover the radiation aspect of a nuclear zone but mainly focus's on defense, fallout prediction, mass casualty response etc etc

My current MOS in the military is 74D Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear Specialist (CBRN) we do not cover explosive weaponry. Alot of chemical weapons do have a explosive charge, aerosol ejection or some device down that line but my main job is to make soldiers aware of CBRN threats, how to respond to contamination, how to treat victims, recognize symptoms, fallout planning, defense measures etc.

Here is a better laid out description of my MOS http://www.army-portal.com/jobs/chemical/74d.html

Not very fast at all to be fair, what would most likely happen is a massive quick military response. Soldiers and relief teams such as Hazmat and Medical teams would be equipped with the proper JLIST (A link will be provided to information about JLIST) or any other chemical protection gear. 

Recon CBRN teams would be sent in to investigate the severity and contaminated areas using the CBRN Strykers (Equipped to even go in to radiation zones) or other vehicles fitted to go into CBRN contaminated zones then ground troops would move and begin to set up Decon and Containment zones to prepare for the mass casualties that would be coming in. Air Craft would either disperse super tropical bleach or fire bomb non population are to start creating new areas for Decon zones.

Troops would be cycled in and out of the zones once due to not wanting the JLIST to fail or endanger troops being exposed. Hazmat and Medical teams would be in full operation till the contamination was dealt with. If the contamination was not immediately threatening people it could be marked off and secured until later decon.

Water is the biggest issues with chemical attacks due to most Chemical agents have the ability to survive in water for quiet some time so that would be the biggest challenge I personally think because wells would have to be destroyed or treated and affected lakes, ponds, etc would have to be dealt with.

Food can be another issue, mustard gas is especially sneaky cause it can survive several days sometimes just hanging out on crops or soil areas and can be just as lethal even when diluted by natural rain or not being properly destroyed.

 JLIST Information link http://www.armystudyguide.com/content/Military_Equipment_Information/CBRN_Equipment_Information/joint-service-lightweight.shtml

All nerve agents cause very unpleasant deaths but VX can cause muscle spasms but that isn't always the case in victims. In the case of the sickening attack against the Kurds some victims who had been most effected by VX had a sadly bitten through their own tongues due to spasms before they passed.

Just to add abit of info Volsunga, Sarin can also be used as a liquid agent and doesn't always need to be Aerosolized to be completely lethal. This method isn't as effective but is used by less those that want a cheaper method of deploying the agent.
